title: Perkins' instruments and the location of his studio
summary: Perkins' main instrument was bass; he kept many instruments for pupils at his house on 6th Street.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I wanted to ask a little bit more about Perkins. What was his main instrument when he took a job and played in bands? What?
Well his main instrument that I know was the bass.
Yeah, he had a horn like mine but it was a four-valve bass. It had four valves. And it was an E flat.
Did you ever see him play drums any time?
Well no, no more than teaching the fellas around his house.
The trombone, he had the trombone. He kept all those instruments that the scholars would like, they would come, he'd have all those instruments hanging on the side of the wall.
I wanted to ask about a studio. Where was that 6th Street?

That's, uh, Mr. Russell I really don't know, I really don't know the number of that house. But it's on 6th between Dryde and Barone on the uptown side of the street. And it's about the second house from Barone Street coming toward Dryde's.
We never got to know him of course so I was curious.
No, he passed, he passed oh long years ago. Let me see now. I really don't know exactly the year that he passed. What was he like?
